result.title: Whose Credential Is It? How Owner Attribution in Agent MemoryShapes Cross-User Account Misuse
result.summary: Shared long-term memory lets an LLM agent serving one user inadvertently retrieve another user's credentials, but it is unclear when such exposure leads to actual harm. We introduce a three-stage audit that separates three events: a foreign credential reaches the prompt (exposure), the agent acts with it (behavior), and the other user's account changes (state). In AppWorld, a store that mixes 763 past logins from all users retrieves another user's credential for 84.7 percent of required apps, yet agents rarely act on it. Misuse appears in a stress test where memory lacks the user's own credential and presents a single foreign one as the user's record: seven agents then use it in 80 to 94 percent of runs and change the victim's account in up to 43 percent, sometimes passing the official check. Naming the owner before or inside each credential line prevents most of this: with all else fixed, misuse falls from 92 to 1 of 305 paired runs, also with name-free usernames, though owner-bound notes cost 3 to 5 successful tasks per model on clean memory. A wrongly written owner largely restores misuse; trailing owner tags and added safety instructions help only some models. Agent memory should consistently record whose credential it stores, and evaluations should measure behavior, not only exposure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出三阶段审计，把「他人凭据进入提示」「agent 实际据其行动」「受害者账户状态改变」分开测量，在 AppWorld 中考察共享长期记忆导致的跨用户凭据误用，并发现逐条标注凭据所有者能大幅降低误用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将「信息出现在上下文」与「模型是否真正使用它」分离的审计与配对干预设计，可能启发 LVR 中区分 latent 表示可用性与实际因果贡献、以及用行为而非可用性做评价的问题，可供核查；但与视觉推理领域相距较远。
